Thanks for the ping — quick read attached (Redline_Notes_KP.pdf). Top-line thoughts: 

1) Hosting / residency ask: reasonable to commit to EU-region processing for customer-designated workloads, but only when customer selects Dedicated or Private deployment (we cannot guarantee region for shared-hosted tier without contractual routing guarantees). Suggested compromise language: commit to offer EU-only processing for workloads designated in the Order Form; for hosted accounts, include best-effort routing plus notice and migration support.

2) Subprocessors: quarterly notifications are operationally heavy. We can accept quarterly disclosure of material changes (new infra/major subprocessor) and keep the rolling registry updated monthly; emergency notices for critical changes.

3) SOC / evidence timeline: 60 days is tight — we can commit to delivering SOC-related evidence within 60 business days for production incidents where evidence exists, and standard SOC reports annually. If they need faster on-boarding evidence, offer a "one-off" expedited packet at cost.

4) Liability carve-outs tied to residency: push back. We should not accept unlimited carve-outs; propose a narrowly scoped credit remedy for failure to meet region commitments, capped to fees for affected services in the prior 6 months.

5) SCCs: we have a Redwood-verified SCC package. Recommend we reference our SCCs but include a transfer impact addendum for country-specific restrictions — careful to avoid language that creates an absolute transfer ban that could block service.

Recommendation: consolidate most positions in the DPA except residency routing specifics and credits — those can be handled as Order Form terms (commercial). I attached suggested redline snippets in the PDF.

If Oxbridge insists on EU-only for hosted, we should ask Product whether we can offer an SLA or a technical routing guarantee; otherwise decline.

If you want, I can draft a consolidated response to Sara and Anil that proposes Redwood positions and offers a 30-min alignment call.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Sara / Anil — thanks for sending the redlines and for the clarity on timelines. Attached is a consolidated Redwood response (Redwood_Proposed_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx) that: 

- Accepts SCCs as the baseline transfer mechanism and attaches our standard SCC package; includes a short transfer-impact addendum that preserves our ability to route workloads across regions unless the Order Form specifically designates an EU-only environment.
- Commits to quarterly notification of material subprocessor changes and a live subprocessors registry updated monthly; emergency notifications for critical changes.
- Commits to delivering SOC/evidence in an expedited packet for onboarding or incident contexts (60 business days where evidence exists); annual SOC reports otherwise.
- Proposes a narrowly scoped credit remedy for failure to meet EU-designated routing when the Order Form specifies EU-only processing (cap: fees for service over prior 6 months). We declined a full liability carve-out but offer the credit remedy as practical recourse.

We prefer to keep specifics of routing (how and when migrations occur) in the Order Form, and have captured suggested snippets in the attached docx. If that approach is acceptable, we can finalize language and issue a single redlined DPA for signature.

We are available for a 30-min alignment call with your counsel on Thu 16 Dec between 09:00-11:00 GMT or 14:00-16:00 GMT. Please confirm a slot if you'd like to take the call.

Next steps per Redwood:
- If you confirm the EU-designation approach, Redwood will produce an Order Form addendum template to capture the routing details.
- I'll circulate final redlines after call (if any) and we can push to DocuSign.
